summary.headline: BirlaNu Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore; standalone EBITDA margin up ~380 bps, but Parador impairment of Rs 74 crore hit standalone books.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year, with subdued demand, pricing pressure and Middle East-driven volatility. Q4 improved: consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore and standalone EBITDA margin expanded about 380 bps, helped by a Rs 5 crore Clean Coats dividend and resin price spikes in March. Full-year consolidated revenue was Rs 3,730 crore (+3%), while standalone EBITDA rose 39% to Rs 146 crore, aided by Rs 22 crore Clean Coats dividend and Rs 7 crore asset-sale profit. A Rs 74 crore diminution provision on the BirlaNu International GmbH (Parador) investment was booked as an exceptional item in standalone accounts, and Parador posted a Rs 35 crore operating loss in Q4 including a Rs 19 crore severance provision. Total debt was Rs 851 crore at year-end, down from Rs 929 crore in December.

segments.name: Roofs
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 275 crore (+8% YoY, +18% QoQ); FY26 revenue broadly stable at Rs 1,139 crore. Management says it holds market leadership and pricing premium, with margins largely stable.

segments.name: Walls
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 161 crore (+14% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 610 crore (+13%). Mix about 60% AAC Blocks, 25% Panels, 15% Boards; Panels and Boards grew 20-25% in FY26; Q4 blended volume growth above 20%. Blocks, Panels and Boards are all at full capacity utilisation.

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 37 crore (+58% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 117 crore (+45%), crossing Rs 100 crore milestone. Ex-Clean Coats growth was 25% for FY26; Clean Coats contributed Rs 20 crore over 4.5 months since acquisition.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 147 crore (+4% YoY, ~+30% QoQ per CEO); FY26 revenue Rs 495 crore (-8%) with flat volumes. Q4 EBITDA margin up ~1,300 bps YoY on March resin price spike and inventory revaluation; FY26 margin up 280 bps. CPVC ~39-40% of mix, uPVC/SWR/pressure pipes the rest; Q4 volume growth about 2-3%.

segments.name: Parador (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 9% YoY in euro terms in Q4 and 7% for FY26; operating loss Rs 35 crore in Q4 including Rs 19 crore severance. Management expects gradual recovery through FY27 from retail reboot and premium Engineered Wood range.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Pipes to see a stronger recovery in FY27, supported by government spending and infrastructure demand; resin prices expected to stabilise over coming months.
Parador: expects sales bounce-back in FY27 with positive profitability flow-through; no quantified target given.
Brownfield Walls capacity expansions expected to come on-stream within FY27 (around Q3 at latest); Nellore greenfield boards plant (HD and designer boards) on track.
BCG value enhancement savings expected to be fully realised from FY27 onwards.
Management aspires to double-digit EBITDA margins via portfolio mix shift toward Construction Chemicals and Walls; no timeline given beyond 2-3 years.
Roofs: price differential versus steel roofing is high, giving pricing headroom and substitution opportunity; some input-cost inflation expected to be partly offset by price increases.
capex_capacity: Nellore, Andhra Pradesh greenfield boards plant is on track against defined execution milestones; will add value-added HD and designer boards.
OPVC facility in Patna is fully commissioned.
Brownfield Walls expansions expected to come on-stream in FY27, hopefully by start or around Q3.
Pipes: capacity to scale a further 30-40% over current output without fresh investment; footprint across North, South, East and West India; over 3,000 SKUs.
Walls: Chennai new line utilisation improved during FY26.
demand_pricing: Roofs: management cites good demand momentum over the last 2-3 months, better than the last couple of years, with rural resilience and substitution away from steel roofing as steel prices rallied.
Pipes: PVC resin prices hit multiyear lows, then rose about 60% in March over 3-4 weeks and a further 25-30% in April; government spending on water/JJM showed early green shoots from Q4.
Parador: weak European demand, intensified competition and softer pricing; Engineered Wood mid-end hit by cheaper Chinese imports, so premium range launched in February.
Middle East conflict drove energy and logistics volatility, rupee depreciation and imported raw material inflation; some orders deferred from March into FY27.
Pricing pressure persisted in Walls through FY26, offset by cost discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Given the Parador impairment, when will the company take a final call on the European subsidiary after about 8 years of losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is applying external advisers' recommended actions at Parador, some visible and some not, and acts on data and order books rather than hope; no specific exit decision was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Construction Chemicals growth including and excluding Clean Coats?
qa_highlights.answer: Including Clean Coats, FY26 growth was 45% and Q4 growth 58%; excluding Clean Coats, FY26 growth was 25%. Clean Coats contributed Rs 20 crore over 4.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Pipes product mix and the anti-dumping duty removal?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC is about 39-40% of pipes mix and uPVC and other products the rest. Management said the duty removal was a government step taken in early April to curb volatility; it declined to comment on industry lobbying.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Parador's Q4 margin so negative beyond severance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no other operational issues; the loss was mainly lower revenue and volumes as orders deferred after the early-March war disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How is Parador positioned in India and against lower-priced competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Positioned at the premium end as a Made in Germany product, targeting metros and large cities with a dedicated sales team; landed cost and price sensitivity were flagged as challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt capacity and the impact of the employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said consolidated equity is about Rs 1,100 crore against debt of about Rs 850 crore, with room for another Rs 200-250 crore. Management said the employee cost comparison needs reconciliation and that headcount is reviewed constantly.

qa_highlights.question: Walls volume growth, capacity utilisation and segment mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 Walls blended volume growth above 20%; Blocks, Panels and Boards all at full utilisation; mix about 60% Blocks, 25% Panels, 15% Boards.

risks_watch: Parador: further impairments or severance in FY27, and whether European sales recover as management expects.
Pipes: PVC resin price volatility, reversal of the March spike, and the anti-dumping duty removal ending June; channel stocking or destocking risk.
Standalone margin sustainability: Q4 benefited from one-offs (Clean Coats dividend Rs 5 crore, inventory revaluation, asset-sale gains).

Balance sheet: debt at Rs 851 crore; management indicated capacity for Rs 200-250 crore more; inorganic growth and $1 billion revenue ambition may require equity or cash accrual support, and the promoter stance was not addressed.
Input cost inflation from rupee depreciation, freight, cement, fibre and energy; pricing pass-through in Roofs is not yet confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India operations and Q4 momentum, especially Pipes and Walls, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Parador's future, the impairment and capital allocation. Management repeatedly deferred to 'external advisers' and 'timing' without giving quantified targets.
key_quotes: I am happy to say we enter FY27 with a strong momentum on both growth and profitability and the evidence of that comes from our performance in Q4 for the India business.
We react on data and lead indicators and what the order books and pipelines are.
So, without Clean Coats, the growth is 25% for full year. With Clean Coats, it is 58%.
